statement: The function returns a result r, len(r) = n, and for every city i with 1 <= i <= n, r[i-1] equals the minimum of (1+k)*d(i,j) + appleCost[j-1] over all cities j with 1 <= j <= n that are reachable from i in the undirected graph whose edges are the roads; here d(u,v) is the least total road cost of any route from city u to city v, with d(u,u)=0. Equivalently, r[i-1] is the least possible total cost of starting at city i, traveling to some city j, buying exactly one apple there for appleCost[j-1], and returning to i while every road cost on the return trip is multiplied by k.
preconditions: Problem constraints hold: 2 <= n <= 1000; roads is a list of length m with 1 <= m <= 2000; each roads[t] is a 3-element vector [a_t,b_t,c_t] with 1 <= a_t,b_t <= n, a_t != b_t, and 1 <= c_t <= 100000; no unordered pair of cities occurs as the endpoints of two different roads; appleCost has length n and 1 <= appleCost[j] <= 100000 for every 0 <= j < n; 1 <= k <= 100.
